cards.explanation: The answer is by the will of God. Right there in the opening line, Paul says he is “…an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God…” (Ephesians 1:1). He doesn't say he earned the title or campaigned for it. I've seen plenty of people puff up a job title, and Paul hands the credit upward instead, friends. That's a good way to start a letter.

The answer is Christ. Paul says God “…has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly realms.” (Ephesians 1:3). Notice the little words "in Christ." Paul comes back to them again and again in this passage. Every spiritual blessing, and they're all found in Him.

The answer is holy and blameless in His presence. Paul says God chose us “…to be holy and blameless in His presence.” (Ephesians 1:4). Look at where that happens, friends: in His presence. And the choosing happened before the foundation of the world.

The answer is adoption as His sons. Paul says God “…predestined us for adoption as His sons through Jesus Christ…” (Ephesians 1:5). Adoption means being brought into a family. I think that's why this word hits so warm. It comes through Jesus Christ, and Paul ties it to the good pleasure of God's will.

The answer is True. Verse 4 ends with the words “In love,” and verse 5 runs right on: “He predestined us for adoption as His sons through Jesus Christ…” (Ephesians 1:4-5). So the predestining happens in love. Paul doesn't give it any other setting. I think that's a lovely thing to see tucked at the end of a verse.

The answer is His glorious grace. Paul says it is “…to the praise of His glorious grace, which He has freely given us in the Beloved One.” (Ephesians 1:6). Freely given is how Paul puts it, friends. Then he goes on, “In Him we have redemption through His blood…” (Ephesians 1:7). The Beloved One is where it all comes from.

The answer is forgiveness. Paul says, “In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses…” (Ephesians 1:7). Forgiveness. I know what it is to feel stuck in the dark, and this word is the light coming in. And Paul says it's according to the riches of His grace.

The answer is False. The text says the opposite of sparingly. Paul writes of “…the riches of His grace that He lavished on us with all wisdom and understanding.” (Ephesians 1:7-8). Lavished means poured out, not rationed. That's a generous God.

The answer is that God made it known to us. Paul says, “And He has made known to us the mystery of His will according to His good pleasure…” (Ephesians 1:9). A mystery that God hands over to us, friends. That's a mystery with the lights turned on. It isn't kept in a locked drawer.

The answer is that the plan brings all things in heaven and on earth together in Christ. Paul says it is “…a plan for the fullness of time, to bring all things in heaven and on earth together in Christ.” (Ephesians 1:10). All things, both heaven and earth, brought together. It's a very big plan. And it all centers on Christ.

The answer is for the praise of His glory. Paul says it is “…in order that we, who were the first to hope in Christ, would be for the praise of His glory.” (Ephesians 1:12). The point lands on God's glory, friends. Not on the ones who were chosen. I find that humbling, and I think it takes the pressure off.

The answer is False. The sealing comes after the hearing. Paul says, “And in Him, having heard and believed the word of truth…” and then, “…you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit…” (Ephesians 1:13). So they heard the gospel first, and believed it. The sealing follows.

The answer is inheritance. Paul says the Holy Spirit “…is the pledge of our inheritance until the redemption of those who are God’s possession, to the praise of His glory.” (Ephesians 1:14). A pledge is like a promise you can hold now. And the inheritance is still being waited on. I like that the Spirit is the pledge.

The answer is True. Paul says the Spirit is the pledge of our inheritance “…until the redemption of those who are God’s possession, to the praise of His glory.” (Ephesians 1:14). So they're God's own possession, friends. That's a happy thing to be called. It's a bit like being a cookie that belongs in the box.
